subject: Social Habits
title: My body belongs to me
subtopics: Saying no and telling a trusted adult
objectives: Children will say "my body is mine" and say "stop" to touch they do not like.
Children will name trusted adults they can tell.
content: My body is mine, saying no and telling a trusted adult, and my safe grown-ups.
teachingActivities: Teach this week gently and briefly using puppets, songs and pictures; use simple words and never describe abuse or ask children questions about what has happened to them; follow the school’s safeguarding and child protection policy and tell parents in advance what is taught; if a child says anything that worries you, listen calmly, do not question, and report it to the designated safeguarding lead the same day; never promise to keep a secret.
learnerActivities: Say "my body is mine", say stop to touch they do not like and name trusted adults they can tell.
resources: Pictures of trusted adults such as teacher, parent and nurse
assessment: Observe whether each child says stop with a hand sign and names a trusted adult. Never assess through personal questions.
expectedOutcomes: Says stop to touch they do not like.

lessons.title: My body is mine
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will learn that their body belongs to them and that they can choose who touches it.
successCriteria: Says my body is mine with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stay safe on the road, ask for help and name feelings.
lessons.starter: Show a puppet and say "This is my body. It is mine. I look after it and I say who can touch it."
teacherActivities: Show the body outline and say "This is your body. It is yours."
Say "You can say stop if you do not like a touch."
Show the puppet saying stop to a tickle and the other puppet stopping.
learnerActivities: Children look and touch their own arm.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the body outline and say "This is your body. It is yours." Children: Children look and touch their own arm.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "You can say stop if you do not like a touch." Children: Children show a stop hand.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the puppet saying stop to a tickle and the other puppet stopping. Children: Children watch and say stop.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "My body is mine." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Stop hand
practical.safety: Use only puppets and pictures and never demonstrate on a child’s body. Keep the tone calm and positive and follow the school’s safeguarding policy.

differentiation.support: Show the stop hand together and say stop.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the puppet to stop.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says my body is mine with a prompt
lessons.conclusion: Sing the body song and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Respect your child’s no to hugs and tickles, and say "Your body is yours."
teacherReflection: Which children could show "learn that their body belongs to them and that they can choose who touches it" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: My body is mine, my body is mine, I can say stop.

lessons.title: Saying no and stop
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: Saying no and telling a trusted adult
objectives: Children will practise saying no and stop to things they do not like and learn to tell an adult.
successCriteria: Says no or stop in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stay safe on the road, ask for help and name feelings.
lessons.starter: Use two puppets: one takes a toy and the other says "No, stop. That is mine."
teacherActivities: Show the puppet saying no and stop to a toy being taken.
Say "If someone does something we do not like, we say stop and tell a grown-up."
Let children practise saying no and stop to a puppet.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the puppet saying no and stop to a toy being taken. Children: Children watch and say stop.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "If someone does something we do not like, we say stop and tell a grown-up." Children: Children repeat tell a grown-up.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children practise saying no and stop to a puppet. Children: Child says no and stop.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "A grown-up will listen." Children: Children nod and smile.

practical.title: No and stop
steps: Say no and stop to the puppet.
practical.safety: Keep the practice about toys and play only and use puppets. If a child says something that worries you, listen calmly and report it to the safeguarding lead the same day.

differentiation.support: Say stop together with a stop hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name who they would tell.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you say if you do not like something?

expectedOutcomes: Says no or stop in play
lessons.conclusion: Show a stop hand and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell your child they can always tell you if something worries them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "practise saying no and stop to things they do not like and learn to tell an adult" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: My safe grown-ups
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name the grown-ups they can tell when they feel worried.
successCriteria: Names or points to a safe grown-up
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stay safe on the road, ask for help and name feelings.
resources: Pictures of a teacher, a parent, a grandparent and a nurse
lessons.starter: Show a hand-shaped chart and say "On each finger, we put a grown-up we can tell."
teacherActivities: Show the trusted adult pictures and name each person.
Help each child choose people they can tell and place stickers on fingers.
Say "I can tell my safe grown-ups."
learnerActivities: Child places a sticker on a finger.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the trusted adult pictures and name each person. Children: Children look and say who.
Step 2. Teacher: Help each child choose people they can tell and place stickers on fingers. Children: Child places a sticker on a finger.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "I can tell my safe grown-ups." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Grown-ups help us stay safe." Children: Children smile.

practical.title: Safe hand chart
practical.safety: Use non-toxic stickers and never ask children questions about their families beyond who helps them. Respect each family’s situation.

differentiation.support: Point to a picture and name the grown-up together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend who their safe grown-ups are.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you do if you are worried?

lessons.conclusion: Hold up the safe hand and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk to your child about who they can tell when they feel worried.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name the grown-ups they can tell when they feel worried" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Safe and happy
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will sing and act songs that reinforce stop, tell and safe grown-ups.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stay safe on the road, ask for help and name feelings.
lessons.starter: Sing the safe song and do the actions for stop and tell.
teacherActivities: Teach the safe song with actions for stop and tell.
Use the puppet to say "I feel safe."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Teach the safe song with actions for stop and tell. Children: Children do the actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the song again slowly. Children: Children sing with the actions.
Step 3. Teacher: Use the puppet to say "I feel safe." Children: Children say I feel safe.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Everyone is safe at school." Children: Children smile and wave.

practical.title: Safe song
practical.safety: Keep the mood warm and light and the actions simple. Never press a child to share personal experiences.

differentiation.support: Do the actions together and sing quietly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead the song.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you say to stop?

lessons.conclusion: Sing the song once more and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing the safe song at home and talk about safe grown-ups.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing and act songs that reinforce stop, tell and safe grown-ups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 safety check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child shows stop and names a safe grown-up.
successCriteria: Shows a stop hand and says stop
Names or points to a safe grown-up
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stay safe on the road, ask for help and name feelings.
lessons.starter: Sing the safe song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: stop, tell and safe grown-ups.
At each station watch how the child responds.
Record each child’s level in a general way only.
learnerActivities: Child responds with a word or sign.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: stop, tell and safe grown-ups. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child responds. Children: Child responds with a word or sign.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level in a general way only. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Safety stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use puppets and pictures only. Record observations only and report any concern to the safeguarding lead.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show a friend the stop hand.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: shows a stop hand; says no or stop in play; names a safe grown-up; says I can tell. Do not question children about their own experiences.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
Shows stop and names a safe grown-up
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep reminding your child that they can tell you anything.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child shows stop and names a safe grown-up" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
